Abstract This comprehensive review summarizes the published liter- ature data concerning the intramolecular Diels–Alder reactions of viny- larenes  (the  IMDAV  reaction)  and  alkynyl  arenes  from  1970  to  2019, and covers mainly intramolecular [4+2] cycloaddition reactions of vinyl- or acetylene-substituted furans, thiophenes, pyrroles, indoles, imidaz- oles, benzenes, and naphthalenes, in which the unsaturated substituent is linked directly to an arene moiety. The selected area of the Diels–Al- der reaction differs from other forms of [4+2] cycloadditions due to the uniqueness of the diene fragment, which, along with an exocyclic multi- ple bond, includes the double bond of an aromatic or heteroaromatic nucleus in its system. Thus, during the formation of the [4+2] cycload- dition intermediate, the aromaticity of furan, thiophene and even ben- zene rings is broken, leading, as a rule, to the formation of heterocyclic structures rarely accessible by other methods, in contrast to the majori- ty of intermolecular Diels–Alder reactions, with the highest degree of chemo-,  regio-,  and  diastereoselectivity.  Therefore,  the  IMDAV  ap- proach is often used for the synthesis of naturally occurring and bioac- tive molecules, which are also discussed in this review alongside other applications of this reaction. Whenever possible, we have tried to avoid examples  of  radical,  photochemical,  oxidative,  precious-metal-com- plex-catalyzed cyclizations  and other  types of formal  [4+2]  cycloaddi- tions,  focusing  on  thermal  Diels–Alder  reactions  in  the  first  step,  ac- cording to the classical mechanism. The second stage of the process, aromatization, is unique for many initial substrates, and hence consid- erable attention in this overview is given to the detailed description of the reaction mechanisms. Synthesis 2021, 53, A–BO Intermediate  cases  of  intramolecular  cyclization  of alkynyl arenes bearing a double bond on the side chain are also the subject of discussion in this work. Despite the fact that this form of cycloaddition reaction has only been in development since the 1970s, considerable experimental  material  has  already  been  accumulated  in more  than  100  reports  over  the  last  forty  years,  which needs to be generalized. It is also important to note that like many  other  cycloaddition  strategies,  due  to  its  versatility and the availability of the starting materials, the IMDAV re- action has become widely used for the synthesis of natural and biologically active substances (in the schemes that fol- low, polycyclic systems of natural compounds will be high- lighted). Therefore, the aim of this review, which embodies the data published between l970 and 2019, is to summarize the  experimental  results  concerning  intramolecular  [4+2] cycloadditions in different classes of vinylarenes, mainly in vinylfurans,  vinylthiophenes,  vinylpyrroles,  vinylindoles, vinylimidazoles, and styrenes, where a multiple bond plays the role of a dienophile. The corresponding sections will be subdivided  according  to  the  type  of  internal  dienophile: alkenes, alkynes, or allenes. 2 IMDAV Reactions of Vinylfurans 2.1 Alkenes as Internal Dienophiles Furans, being one of the least aromatic heterocycles, un- dergo the IMDAV reaction more easily than all other viny- larenes. In this regard, most publications have been devoted to intramolecular [4+2] cycloadditions of 2-vinylfurans. 3- Vinylfurans  are  somewhat  less  available;  however,  many cycloaddition  reactions  involving  their  participation  have been described.

As noted previously (Scheme 1), one of the earliest suc- cessful examples of the intramolecular Diels–Alder reaction of  vinylfurans  was  reported  by  Kotsuki  et  al.  in  1981.5  In this  method,  fumarates  1,  which  are  easily  obtained  from acetylfurans or furfurals, were subjected to heating at 200 °C in the presence of a catalytic amount of hydroquinone as an inhibitor of radical reactions (Scheme 4). This  thermal  cyclization  reaction  produced  benzo[1,2- b:4,5-c′]difurans 3 in good yields, which after catalytic de- hydrogenation, accompanying decarbomethoxylation,5 can be considered as the key intermediates in total syntheses of sesquiterpenoids of the furanoeremophilane family; for ex- ample,  secofuranoeremophilane  and  related  compounds.6 The structures of the lactones were established by NMR and it  was  confirmed  that  the  IMDAV  reaction  proceeded through an exo-[4+2] cycloaddition via the intermediate ad- ducts  2,  in  which  the  trans  configuration  of  the  activated double bond passes unchanged in the products 3. 3-Vinylfurans,  with  the  structure  of  the  dienophilic tether being similar to 2-substituted furans 6 and 8, are also able to enter into the IMDAV reaction. As will be shown be- low, as a rule, the cycloaddition conditions for structurally similar 2-vinyl and 3-vinylfurans (thiophenes, pyrroles and other heterocycles) are not very different. For example, re- action  conditions  similar  to  those  in  Scheme  8  were  em- ployed  for  the  intramolecular  cyclization  of  3-vinylfurans 17 and 19 (Schemes 10 and 11). The simplest of these pathways in- clude an IMDAV reaction as the key step. In 1987, the synthesis of tricycles 25 and 26, which are close analogues of furanoeremophilanes, from furandienes 21 and 22 bearing a masked carbonyl group was described (Scheme 12).8a Furanoeremophilanes are a relatively exten- sive  class  of  furanosesquiterpenes  isolated  from  plants  of the genus Ligularia (family Compositae), and precisely, from the  roots  of  Ligularia  japonica  Less.8b,c  The  intramolecular cycloaddition  of  the  vinylfurans  21  and  22  proceeded  at 240  °C,  leading  to  nitriles  23  and  24  in  moderate  yields. Deprotection of the latter allowed the carbonyl fragment to be  regenerated,  yielding  mixtures  of  diastereomeric  tricy- clic ketones 25 and 26.

Another rapid approach toward heteroanalogues of ma- rine-occurring  furanosesquiterpenes,  isolated  from  a  spe- cies  of  the  sponge  of  the  genus  Dysidea  and  possessing  a high  level  of  biological  activity,9  was  reported  recently  by Tilve and co-workers (Scheme 13 and Table 1).10 The most attractive  feature  of  this  method  is  the  realization  of  a Wittig  olefination/IMDAV  reaction  cascade,  which  allows the synthesis of adducts 32, 33, 35 and 36 from furfurals 27 and 28 under one-pot conditions. Preliminary synthesis of complex phosphoranes (see table 1) 29 and 30, harsh tem- perature conditions (bp of diphenyl ether is 258 °C), and the formation of mixtures of isomeric products in all cases can be considered as disadvantages of this route. A  research  team  from  the  Broad  Institute  of  MIT  and Harvard and the University of Salerno proposed a strategy for  the  synthesis  of  furo[2,3-g]isoquinoline  derivatives  42 and  43  based  on  the  intermolecular  coupling  of  simple building  blocks,  and  was  aimed  at  finding  new  routes  to skeletally  diverse  small molecules  (Scheme  14).11  This ap- proach involves three stages: the first step is a three-com- ponent  Wittig  reaction,  which  leads  stereospecifically  to Scheme 12  The IMDAV approach to the furanoeremophilane core . l a i r e t a m d e t h g i r y p o C the starting aniline 37. The second step is the N-acylation of the secondary amine 37 under the action of chlorides of 2- or 3-furylacrylic acids (38 and 39, respectively).

The final step of  the  transformation  is  the  microwave- assisted Diels–Alder reaction of amides 40 and 41. Attempts to  perform  this  step  using  microwave  irradiation  at  tem- peratures below 200 °C failed, and the reaction only became possible when heating at 250 °C. Furoisoquinolines 42 and 43  were  isolated  in  quite  low  yields  and  the  structures  of both diastereomers were confirmed by X-ray diffraction. In  the  20th  century,  aryl-containing  di-,  tri-  and tetraynes  (specifically,  phenyl  acetylene  derivatives)  were much less explored in IMDAV reactions in comparison with similar  dienes,  trienes,  enynes,  and  related  unsaturated compounds, apparently due to a lack of convenient meth- ods  for  polyyne  preparation.
